title: View or copy a Shared Map
summary: Use a view-only snapshot or make an editable private copy when offered.

evidence: server/src/utils/guideOracleKnowledge.js: reviewed original fact objects at b8345be4d2f7a097e81cb03eef64b473abd0cec9

sections.title: Open a published Shared Map
paragraphs: A published ordinary Shared Map is a view-only snapshot you can open without signing in. You need its current working share link.
steps: Open the published Shared Map link provided by its owner.
Check the map name and browse its map and resource list. Open a resource to read its supplied details.
If you want a print-friendly layout, choose Print-friendly view. On a phone, open the shared map controls menu to find this option.
Confirm time-sensitive details with the resource provider before using them for a visit or registration.
notes: You are viewing the version the owner last published. Later private edits appear only after the owner updates the shared link.
The shared page does not let you add to or edit the owner’s original My Map. Viewing it does not save its resources in your My Directory.
If the link no longer opens, ask the owner for a working published link. It may have been unpublished; signing in does not restore an unavailable snapshot.

sections.title: Make your own private copy when offered
paragraphs: Copy to My Maps creates a separate private map from the published snapshot. You must be signed in with access to My Maps, be a visitor rather than its owner and have this copy option available.
steps: Open the ordinary Shared Map link and review the snapshot you want to copy.
If you are signed out, use Sign in and return to the shared page after signing in to your existing account.
Select Copy to My Maps when it is offered. On a phone, open the shared map controls menu to find it.
Wait for the copy to open as your own My Map. Check its resources and any copied shared notes.
Edit your own copy using its map controls. Keep it private, or deliberately use Share when you later want to publish your version.
notes: Your copy does not change the owner’s original and does not automatically follow later updates to that original. It contains the public snapshot rather than the owner’s private map data.
Copied shared resource notes start private in your new map. Review your own sharing choices before publishing your copy.
Copying a map does not give you permission to edit the providers’ public resource listings.

Copy to My Maps is not offered for every shared-map type: governed shared maps do not support this workflow, and owners already have their original map. If the button is absent, use the view-only page or open the original map you already own. If copying reports an error, check your sign-in and retry only after the problem is resolved.

facts.title: Copy a Shared Map
facts.message: Only the owner can add a saved resource to the original private My Map. Sharing publishes a view-only snapshot; it does not let a visitor add a Place to your original. When Copy to My Maps is available, a signed-in visitor can make a separate private map from the snapshot and edit their copy; it does not change the original map.
